plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-like leaves emerge the following spring and die back by summer. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe and North Africa; naturalized in meadows and woodland edges, and widely grown in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust native perennial with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows, prairies, and roadsides and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to the southern United States
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on New England asters for fuel during their autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful semi-deciduous tree with fern-like foliage that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers just before or as new leaves emerge. It is widely planted as a street and park tree in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November), with some blooms starting in late September
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and subtropical regions worldwide
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas turn the city purple each October, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers hidden among glossy leaves. The scent is often compared to apricots or peaches and can perfume an entire garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to October), with occasional repeat blooms
plants.location: Native to East Asia (China, Japan, Taiwan); widely cultivated in Asia and in warm temperate gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: In China, osmanthus blooms are used to flavor tea, wine, jams, and cakes, and the flowering time is celebrated near the Mid-Autumn Festival in Guilin.
